1: # Sideagent nodes, results and Host continuity
2: 
3: `S` is the `state` command of [lifecycle-state.md](lifecycle-state.md);
4: `execute` and `collect` are in [dispatch-collect.md](dispatch-collect.md).
5: 
6: ## Implementation items
7: 
8: `scope: implementation` is the only scope that admits `mutation: true`.
9: `execute` claims nothing, makes no worktree and touches no forge: the worker's
10: Workflow owns that. Each item sends either its own `prompt` exactly, or the
11: plan's `core` (with `core_revision`) plus the item's `worker_scope`, joined by
12: one blank line; never both. The index row's `prompt_source` keeps the kind,
13: core revision and `sha256:` of core, scope and sent prompt.
14: 
15: With `--state FILE`, an item's `task_id` adds its id to that task's
16: `dispatch` (writer `tool:execute`, no Host revision); an unknown task is
17: `evidence.task_note`. A hold naming the item's `preset` (or `presets`) makes
18: it `not-run` / `on-hold` before any Runner call: a known hold is not probed
19: again. An exactly reconciled prior item stays reconciled.
20: 
21: ## Results
22: 
23: A `collect` result has `excerpt` (480 characters) with `excerpt_truncated`
24: and `reply_chars`; `turn` (holder, prompt fingerprint); `locator` (the Runner
25: `capture` argv `--since <dispatch cursor> --full --inline` and the event log);
26: `output` with its `kind`: `file` (a path, or `{"path": ...}`; checked for
27: presence), `capture` (the reply itself), `remote` (a URL) or `description`
28: (text with spaces); an explicit `{"kind": ...}` wins; and `gaps`:
29: `reply-text-absent`, `capture-truncated`, `output-absent` (a file only). A gap is evidence,
30: not a transport failure. Read the full reply through `locator` before a
31: verdict. A new return resets `acceptance` to `pending` and keeps the earlier
32: value as `prior_acceptance`.
33: 
34: ## Per-assignment dispositions
35: 
36: Task `dispositions` maps item id to `accepted`, `repair`, `cancelled`,
37: `superseded` or `handed-off`. It is Host-owned like `verdict`, which stays the
38: task-level judgment. `$S update --kind tasks ... --index I` mirrors them to the
39: index `acceptance` with `acceptance_source`. After a task verdict, an item of
40: that task without a disposition becomes `undecided` with a note, never left
41: `pending`. A mirror error is reported; the state write stands.
42: 
43: ## Host revision
44: 
45: Each Host business write raises the file's `host_revision` and stamps the
46: record. Tool and Sideagent writes raise nothing and stamp `writer_holder`. The
47: Sideagent view lists `pending_host_changes`: `host:<kind>/<id>@<rev>`,
48: `host:section/<name>@<rev>` and `host:retired/<kind>/<id>@<rev>`.
49: 
50: ## Node mode
51: 
52: Bind `--section sideagent` with `"mode": "node"` and
53: `"recipe": {"runner": "<absolute Runner file>", "argv": ["start", "--repo",
54: "<root>", "--session", "<bound name>", "--role", "sideagent", ...]}` (the
55: checkout `kaola-tmux.sh` takes the platform before `start`), without
56: `--continue` or `--resume` (an optional absolute `state_tool` names
57: `kaola-dispatch.py` when it is not beside the holder or in the sibling Skill). Worker
58: returns and terminations are not node inputs: they reach the Host at its next
59: idle boundary as without a binding, and the Host reads the original. A Host
60: holder advertising `sideagent-node/1` starts a node only for Host business
61: changes past the handled revision, selected when the Host turn has ended, so
62: one turn's writes are one batch. It starts one fresh node from that argv (no
63: shell), sends one prompt with the batch id, the Host revision range and the
64: node's role limits (source pointers only, no restated result, no dispatch or
65: judgment, exact-stop only a Host-recorded reclaim), and reads the node's checkpoint at its turn end. A turn end alone
66: acknowledges nothing. A refused recipe is logged once.
67: 
68: The node writes once:
69: 
70: ```bash
71: $S checkpoint --writer sideagent --source B --batch B --through-host-revision R \
72:   --entries '[{"input":"<id>","applied":["tasks/t1"]},{"input":"<id>","retained":"tasks/t2"}]'
73: ```
74: 
75: `applied` names current records, or `retired:<kind>/<id>`, that this node's
76: holder wrote. `retained` names a current record with `next`, `owner` or `wait`,
77: or a Host `section/<name>`. Older or foreign evidence settles nothing. The
78: result is `maintenance.last_checkpoint`; `last_verified` moves only when every
79: input settled. `acked_host_revision` never passes an unsettled change; a later
80: Host write stays pending. An input the Host rewrote during the batch is
81: `superseded`: its rewrite is the next batch's input. Unsettled inputs go to the Host once, in one
82: `maintenance-returned` alert, and are never sent to another node.
83: 
84: After a verified batch the carrier wakes the Host once, at its next idle
85: boundary, only when an attention item is a record this node wrote and the
86: Host view's attention differs both from what the Host last saw and from the
87: batch's start; otherwise it stays quiet. A partial or
88: missing checkpoint, one whose `through` is below the batch's range, a refused
89: batch, a failed start or a lost node reaches the Host once with the unhandled
90: range; the carrier then exact-stops the node by holder and starts no node for
91: that range again. A failed start or refused batch starts no further node until
92: the binding changes. After `sideagent_node_stop_unconfirmed` no node starts
93: while that holder process still runs. A Host stop in any mode also stops its
94: own node, a start in flight included. A replaced node's late write is
95: `binding-superseded`. There is no timer: the next Host change starts the next
96: node at a Host turn end or the existing idle tick.
97: 
98: ## Host continuity stop
99: 
100: `stop` or `drain-restart` with `--preserve-dispatched-workers` on a Host whose
101: holder advertises `preserve-dispatched/1` keeps each worker tree that Host
102: dispatched (spawn line or a worker record naming its holder) on a cooperative
103: or dead-holder stop; other children are still swept. An older live holder
104: refuses with `preserve-unsupported` and stops nothing: `drain-restart` it at
105: idle first. The successor then runs each seat's `rebind-host`. A start still in
106: flight is not covered: reconcile it. Default stop and final close-out are
107: unchanged; close-out reclaims workers one by one first.
108: 
109: ## Idle wake
110: 
111: A worker's undelivered `idle` wake to its Host is kept like a permission wake
112: and re-sent when the Host is reachable; a newer one replaces it and a stop
113: drops it.
114: 
115: Shown live: fresh nodes on Codex and ZCode, worker survival through a Host
116: preserve stop and rebind on both, and a model-driven Codex Host with a Codex
117: node binding.
118: Not shown live: node mode on the other runtimes.

(End of file - total 118 lines)
</content>

1: # Bounded duty reconciliation
2: 
3: At recovery and before quiescence or closeout, the Host reads applicable owner
4: goal/stop records and relevant newer corrections, comparing authorized duties
5: with actual evidence. Load this reference when a record-visible source/evidence
6: mismatch, an unreconciled latest owner change, genuinely unaccounted coverage
7: after a handoff, or an explicit owner/Delegator request calls for one bounded,
8: read-only Sideagent check. Remembered confidence alone is insufficient. Reuse
9: sufficient unchanged evidence for the same scope and candidate; reuse a check
10: already in flight. A heartbeat, issue completion, compaction, Host replacement
11: or multi-issue closeout alone does not require an audit.
12: 
13: ## Brief and sources
14: 
15: Give the Sideagent the canonical root, affected scope and question, candidate or
16: baseline when relevant, and independent source pointers, not a prefiltered duty
17: list or a conversation/repository dump. It reads applicable requirements before
18: the Host snapshot, using only relevant slices of:
19: 
20: - Latest owner requirements, goal/stop and issue corrections; for a mandate
21:   check include the mandate record (Delegator goal/stop or project plan).
22: - Existing Workflow plans/ledger and delivery, lifecycle and check evidence,
23:   including relevant archived unverified scope/follow-ups for closed issues
24:   within this mandate.
25: - Current Host goal/stop, active/pending and their evidence.
26: 
27: The Delegator retains new owner requirements and source pointers through its
28: existing snapshot/issue handoff. Trusted Delegator records of an owner change
29: remain usable without a raw transcript; disclose uncertainty only where it
30: affects a finding. Missing sources remain explicit uncertainty, never authority
31: to invent work or claim full coverage. A Host-originated duty lost from every
32: available record cannot be reconstructed: this check does not promise perfect
33: recall.
34: 
35: ## Result and Host decision
36: 
37: Return a brief receipt of checked scope, sources read, when, and unavailable
38: sources, followed by concrete findings in these four classes:
39: 
40: - Missing duty.
41: - Unsupported completion claim.
42: - Stale or duplicate pending duty.
43: - Conflict or missing source.
44: 
45: Each finding names its source, evidence or gap, and the smallest proposed
46: correction. Identify the candidate/revision or correction time when material;
47: no required hash/mtime inventory. Later explicit owner corrections win;
48: completed ledger lines are immutable. No record is not proof an action never
49: happened. A change explicitly awaiting relay, work genuinely in flight, or an
50: obligation covered by the current acceptance scope is not missing merely
51: because it lacks a separate row. No findings establishes only the stated scope.
52: 
53: The Host judges each finding and completion, records its decision and remaining
54: duties in its own existing JSON/run records, and assigns any repair under
55: current authorization. The check itself decides no finding, claims no work,
56: grants no permission and accepts no work; the bound Sideagent records only the
57: Host's adopted outcome ([lifecycle-state.md](lifecycle-state.md)). A separate
58: check helper is a counted worker item
59: ([dispatch-collect.md](dispatch-collect.md)); reclaim it when finished, with no
60: idle permanent assistant. Findings use
61: existing QA/Workflow boundaries, not a new approval or completion gate.
62: 
63: ## Independent Delegator inquiry and scheduling
64: 
65: The Delegator may initiate a request during its existing inquiry even when the
66: Host has not requested a check. For example: “Please check this mandate for
67: omitted duties against these goal/stop, correction and run-record pointers;
68: reuse the same in-flight check or sufficient unchanged result.” The sole Host
69: deduplicates and, if needed, assigns an authorized Sideagent. This preserves
70: independent initiation without a second inner-worker controller; an
71: unresponsive Host may delay the check, not transfer control to the Delegator.
72: An interval without a check is not alone a failure or reason for another audit.
73: 
74: Reuse existing Delegator `cadence`, `timer_owner` and the static Skill/project
75: entry: the single native timer wakes an inquiry, not an unconditional Sideagent
76: every interval. This gives the owner a recurring opportunity for independent
77: reconciliation while preserving scoped pauses, current authorization and Host
78: identity recovery under the existing snapshot/handoff rules.
79: 
80: ## Owner changes at a decision boundary
81: 
82: Direct Delegator relay owns delivery: idle send, native noninterrupting steer
83: when supported, otherwise retain until idle. Urgent scoped stop/revocation
84: uses the existing immediate interrupt route; never delay for Sideagent or reads.
85: A trusted relay needs no verbatim quote. Missing/unreadable Delegator snapshot
86: means absent/unknown, not proof of no Delegator or no changes; direct relay works.
87: 
88: At a relevant claim, dispatch, plan adoption or acceptance, Host may read
89: relevant pending changes in the existing Delegator snapshot, without waiting
90: for its timer or mechanically sweeping every state. Delegator alone retains
91: scoped source-backed changes in its own snapshot until adoption is evidenced;
92: Host alone adopts into its body. Delegator observes that evidence and confirms
93: or compacts its record. Neither writes the other's file.
94: 
95: Admission, end-turn, file read or Sideagent receipt alone proves no adoption.
96: An ordinary scoped adopted value/duty with source correlation can suffice
97: without an extra reply. Identical values do not prove a one-shot action ran;
98: urgent stops require actual cessation evidence. Keep independent pending
99: actions and partial effects, not one scalar or an exactly-once claim.
100: 
101: Authority/scope precede time. Later explicit owner direction may supersede
102: earlier direction, including reauthorization after a stop. Stale drafts
103: cannot overwrite newer grants or runtime revocation. Re-evaluate only affected
104: items. Recover ambiguous sends, partial fan-out and interrupted Host/Sideagent
105: from existing records before replaying admitted work; unaffected authorized
106: work continues. No new queue, marker/revision protocol, ledger or scheduler.

(End of file - total 106 lines)

1: # Lifecycle state
2: 
3: `<project>/.kaola/heartbeat-prompt.json` schema `kaola-heartbeat-prompt/2`
4: holds current tasks, the adopted authorization projection, the Sideagent
5: binding, holds, alerts and pending decisions. Its `body` is the generated Host
6: view, not a second source. Change it only through `state` in
7: `scripts/kaola-dispatch.py`; a hand edit skips revision checks. The Delegator
8: file, dispatch index, Runner receipts, Git, forge and Workflow keep their own
9: facts; state keeps references, current conclusions and next steps, never a
10: copied backlog, ledger or history.
11: 
12: ## Roles
13: 
14: - Host: goal, task split, needed abilities, dependencies, preset choice,
15:   assignment text, `execute`/`collect`, reading original results, acceptance
16:   and closeout decisions; bootstrap, failure and urgent recovery. It may read,
17:   search, analyze and do simple authorized work itself.
18: - Tools record dispatch, result and holder facts; no node restates them.
19: - Sideagent: one maintenance role per project, outside every Class seat; a
20:   fresh node per meaningful batch. It reconciles duties, holds, alerts,
21:   conflicts and reclaim, and exact-stops finished workers. It assigns, grants
22:   and accepts nothing. Launches use bypass permissions; a residual prompt is an
23:   exception, and anything needing the user stays a pending `decisions` record.
24: - Research, QA or implementation helpers are counted, authorized items.
25: - Workers never write state (`writer-refused`).
26: 
27: No synchronous Sideagent round trip or approval stage per action: coalesce
28: related updates and reuse valid evidence. The Host gets outcomes, capacity and
29: pending decisions; evidence stays by reference.
30: 
31: ## Commands
32: 
33: `S="python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/kaola-dispatch.py state"`. Every write takes
34: `--file "$PROJECT/.kaola/heartbeat-prompt.json" --writer host|sideagent
35: --source "<event, receipt or Host turn>"`.
36: 
37: - `$S init [--project JSON] [--authorization JSON]`: Host only; refuses an
38:   existing file (migrate it).
39: - `$S update --kind tasks|holds|alerts|decisions --id ID --set PATCH
40:   [--expect-rev N]`: JSON merge patch of one record (`null` deletes a key;
41:   `@path` reads a file). An existing record needs `--expect-rev`; a stale one
42:   exits 3 with `current` and `unapplied`: merge by evidence and retry, never
43:   rewrite the file. `--coalesce` counts a repeated alert.
44: - `$S update --section project|authorization|sideagent|recovery|unverified
45:   --expect-revision N --set PATCH`: first three Host-only.
46: - `$S retire --kind K --id ID --expect-rev N --evidence REF [--outcome T]
47:   [--index I --live L] [--handoff TASK]`: a task needs verdict `accepted` or
48:   `cancelled`, its dispatch items closed and seats stopped, or handed to a
49:   continuing `TASK`.
50: - `$S view --role host|sideagent|delegator [--repo ROOT]` (read-only).
51: - `$S checkpoint`, `update --index`: [sideagent-node.md](sideagent-node.md).
52: - `$S check [--index I] [--live L] [--repo R]`: read-only problems such as
53:   `doing-untraced`, `done-not-retired`, `transcription-unechoed`,
54:   `sideagent-not-live`, `carrier-unproven`.
55: - `$S migrate [--index I] [--live L] [--repo R] [--write]`; `$S timer`
56:   is the Delegator's.

59: 
60: - `tasks` (stable id; `stage` `todo|doing|review|closeout|done`, `goal`):
61:   `source`, `scope`, `needs`, `depends`, `acceptance`, `keep_open`, `wait`,
62:   `dispatch` (index item ids), `evidence`, `next`, `verdict`, `dispositions`
63:   (per item). A repair keeps the task id; one returned branch is not
64:   completion. A task needs no issue; Workflow owners keep claim/ledger/finalize.
65: - `holds` (`scope`, `reason`): `evidence`, `impact`, `owner`, `resume_when`,
66:   `next`. A hold keeps the grant; no takeover or quota reset lifts it.
67: - `alerts` (`level` `watch|warn|severe`, `summary`): level by evidence and
68:   impact, never by elapsed time. Read, acknowledged or in progress is not
69:   resolved; a warning blocks no unrelated work.
70: - `decisions` (`owner` `host|delegator|user`, `question`): kept until
71:   `status: settled` with evidence (Sideagent: with `--host-turn`); a
72:   notification clears no duty.
73: 
74: Authorization, occupancy, task stage and service availability stay separate
75: facts. A stopped process deletes no task.
76: 
77: ## Touchpoints
78: 
79: Update at existing events only: dispatch (task `doing`; plan items carry
80: `task_id`, `output`, optional `requires`), result and verdict, a material
81: goal, grant or fault change, recovery or adoption, and closeout. The inquiry
82: and `check` catch omissions.
83: 
84: ## Host verdicts
85: 
86: `verdict.value` (`accepted|partial|repair|cancelled`) and the Host-owned task
87: fields (`goal`, `scope`, `acceptance`, `needs`, `depends`, `source`,
88: `keep_open`) are Host decisions. The Sideagent records one only with
89: `--host-turn <the Host turn it copies>`; the next Host view lists it under
90: `attention` until the Host writes that task. The Host corrects a wrong
91: transcription with its own `update` (also the bootstrap and degraded path).
92: Partial acceptance keeps the unfinished scope open; moving a `repair` or
93: `partial` task back to `review` keeps that verdict as `prior_verdict` and asks
94: again. A task at `closeout` or `done` without `accepted`, `partial` or
95: `cancelled` stays under `attention` (`verdict-missing`).
96: 
97: ## Sideagent binding
98: 
99: The Host starts the Sideagent, then sets `--section sideagent`
100: `{"platform","session","preset","state":"active"}`; the started Sideagent may
101: add its own `holder_instance_id` once. A reply ending is not the duty's end. To
102: replace, the Host marks `replacing` or `failed`, starts a successor under a new
103: name and binds it; the successor continues from state, index and receipts and
104: replays no admitted work. A Sideagent stop spares each worker it dispatched
105: (spawn line or its record's `dispatcher`); a superseded seat's late write is
106: `binding-superseded`. The Host, not a failed Sideagent, repairs its record and
107: holds it. If both fail, the Delegator recovers the Host first.
108: 
109: ## Events
110: 
111: `execute` records the real dispatcher (`KAOLA_ACP_DISPATCHER`) apart from the
112: notify target. Workers the bound Sideagent starts report to its live Host
113: holder (`sideagent-host`). A Host holder advertising `sideagent-relay/1` relays
114: them to the live bound Sideagent, which confirms at turn end and wakes the Host
115: only when attention changed; a busy Sideagent keeps them; a dead one, or a
116: failed or cancelled Sideagent turn, returns them to the Host. Delivery is
117: at-least-once, a wake hint: rebuild from index and receipts. `"mode": "node"`
118: keeps events with the Host; a node takes a turn's Host changes ([sideagent-node.md](sideagent-node.md)).
119: After a Host replacement (`--preserve-dispatched-workers`), the new Host runs
120: the seat's `rebind-host` from its own session: only that seat's carrier moves;
121: the worker runs on, its `dispatcher` still the old Host. Each seat (Sideagent
122: too) needs its own call; events staged in a dead Host need adoption.
123: `unknown-op`: `drain-restart` the seat at idle.
124: 
125: ## Size
126: 
127: Repeats update the same id. A retired record leaves a capped tombstone; a late
128: event gets `record-retired`. Never drop an open duty to fit. The Host view is
129: bounded at 64 KiB (`host-view-too-large`). The file may reach 1 MiB only with a
130: recorded `carrier` advertising `heartbeat-state/2`, else 64 KiB
131: (`carrier-limit`).
132: 
133: ## Migration
134: 
135: After a Skill update, at a safe point, run `$S migrate --index I --live L`;
136: without `--write` it only plans. With `--write`, each v1 `active` row becomes
137: a `doing` task with its assignment and fields kept, `pending` keeps its stated
138: stage or stays `todo`, `recovery` and the v1 host are kept, a pending row's
139: unknown keys stay inert under `legacy`, and other unknown keys, unassociated
140: index rows and an unproven Sideagent binding become `unverified`. The live
141: Host holder's features become `carrier`. The raw v1 file is kept once as
142: `heartbeat-prompt.v1-<sha12>.json`; a different copy alerts
143: `state-overwritten`. An unknown schema is refused. A repeat reports `current`
144: and still records an upgraded carrier. Migration resets no task, replays no
145: dispatch, re-plans nothing, re-asks no confirmed requirement, restarts no
146: healthy session, grants nothing.
147:

149: across holder death, timer read-back, real state size.

58: ## Records
59: 
60: - `tasks` (stable id; `stage` `todo|doing|review|closeout|done`, `goal`):
61:   `source`, `scope`, `needs`, `depends`, `acceptance`, `keep_open`, `wait`,
62:   `dispatch` (index item ids), `evidence`, `next`, `verdict`, `dispositions`
63:   (per item). A repair keeps the task id; one returned branch is not
64:   completion. A task needs no issue; Workflow owners keep claim/ledger/finalize.
65: - `holds` (`scope`, `reason`): `evidence`, `impact`, `owner`, `resume_when`,
66:   `next`. A hold keeps the grant; no takeover or quota reset lifts it.
67: - `alerts` (`level` `watch|warn|severe`, `summary`): level by evidence and
68:   impact, never by elapsed time. Read, acknowledged or in progress is not
69:   resolved; a warning blocks no unrelated work.
70: - `decisions` (`owner` `host|delegator|user`, `question`): kept until
71:   `status: settled` with evidence (Sideagent: with `--host-turn`); a
72:   notification clears no duty.
73: 
74: Authorization, occupancy, task stage and service availability stay separate
75: facts. A stopped process deletes no task.

77: ## Touchpoints
78: 
79: Update at existing events only: dispatch (task `doing`; plan items carry
80: `task_id`, `output`, optional `requires`), result and verdict, a material
81: goal, grant or fault change, recovery or adoption, and closeout. The inquiry
82: and `check` catch omissions.
83: 
84: ## Host verdicts
85: 
86: `verdict.value` (`accepted|partial|repair|cancelled`) and the Host-owned task
87: fields (`goal`, `scope`, `acceptance`, `needs`, `depends`, `source`,
88: `keep_open`) are Host decisions. The Sideagent records one only with
89: `--host-turn <the Host turn it copies>`; the next Host view lists it under
90: `attention` until the Host writes that task. The Host corrects a wrong
91: transcription with its own `update` (also the bootstrap and degraded path).
92: Partial acceptance keeps the unfinished scope open; moving a `repair` or
93: `partial` task back to `review` keeps that verdict as `prior_verdict` and asks
94: again. A task at `closeout` or `done` without `accepted`, `partial` or
95: `cancelled` stays under `attention` (`verdict-missing`).
96: 
97: ## Sideagent binding
98: 
99: The Host starts the Sideagent, then sets `--section sideagent`
100: `{"platform","session","preset","state":"active"}`; the started Sideagent may
101: add its own `holder_instance_id` once. A reply ending is not the duty's end. To
102: replace, the Host marks `replacing` or `failed`, starts a successor under a new
103: name and binds it; the successor continues from state, index and receipts and
104: replays no admitted work. A Sideagent stop spares each worker it dispatched
105: (spawn line or its record's `dispatcher`); a superseded seat's late write is
106: `binding-superseded`. The Host, not a failed Sideagent, repairs its record and
107: holds it. If both fail, the Delegator recovers the Host first.
108: 
109: ## Events
110: 
111: `execute` records the real dispatcher (`KAOLA_ACP_DISPATCHER`) apart from the
112: notify target. Workers the bound Sideagent starts report to its live Host
113: holder (`sideagent-host`). A Host holder advertising `sideagent-relay/1` relays
114: them to the live bound Sideagent, which confirms at turn end and wakes the Host
115: only when attention changed; a busy Sideagent keeps them; a dead one, or a
116: failed or cancelled Sideagent turn, returns them to the Host. Delivery is
117: at-least-once, a wake hint: rebuild from index and receipts. `"mode": "node"`
118: keeps events with the Host; a node takes a turn's Host changes ([sideagent-node.md](sideagent-node.md)).
119: After a Host replacement (`--preserve-dispatched-workers`), the new Host runs
120: the seat's `rebind-host` from its own session: only that seat's carrier moves;
121: the worker runs on, its `dispatcher` still the old Host. Each seat (Sideagent
122: too) needs its own call; events staged in a dead Host need adoption.
123: `unknown-op`: `drain-restart` the seat at idle.
124: 
125: ## Size
126: 
127: Repeats update the same id. A retired record leaves a capped tombstone; a late
128: event gets `record-retired`. Never drop an open duty to fit. The Host view is
129: bounded at 64 KiB (`host-view-too-large`). The file may reach 1 MiB only with a
130: recorded `carrier` advertising `heartbeat-state/2`, else 64 KiB
131: (`carrier-limit`).
132: 
133: ## Migration
134: 
135: After a Skill update, at a safe point, run `$S migrate --index I --live L`;
136: without `--write` it only plans. With `--write`, each v1 `active` row becomes
137: a `doing` task with its assignment and fields kept, `pending` keeps its stated
138: stage or stays `todo`, `recovery` and the v1 host are kept, a pending row's
139: unknown keys stay inert under `legacy`, and other unknown keys, unassociated
140: index rows and an unproven Sideagent binding become `unverified`. The live
141: Host holder's features become `carrier`. The raw v1 file is kept once as
142: `heartbeat-prompt.v1-<sha12>.json`; a different copy alerts
143: `state-overwritten`. An unknown schema is refused. A repeat reports `current`
144: and still records an upgraded carrier. Migration resets no task, replays no
145: dispatch, re-plans nothing, re-asks no confirmed requirement, restarts no
146: healthy session, grants nothing.

4: ---
5: 
6: # dsh Kaola Project Runner
7: 
8: This Skill is a communication driver for dsh. It gives the controlling Agent a
9: measured ACP channel to one exact owned session; it does not choose commands, Workflow modes, cadence, state, approvals,
10: retries, or completion policy. The separate Skill `kaola-project-runner` (display name Project
11: Runner) is the main orchestrator when a host Agent is supervising workers; this Skill stays
12: transport-only.
13: 
14: ## Transport
15: 
16: ACP is the only transport (Issue #130). The ACP command is `dsh --profile acp`; prompts travel over its stdio JSON-RPC, never shell eval. There is no login step (authMethods is empty); a provider route still needs its credential, such as DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. This platform's ACP quirks are in [references/acp.md](references/acp.md) — open it when a quirk matters. A request for the retired PTY transport is refused with `transport-pty-retired` and changes nothing.
17: 
18: | `mutation_status` | Safe interpretation |
19: |---|---|
20: | `not_started` | No prompt write began. |
21: | `accepted` | The agent accepted the prompt. |
22: | `in_progress` | Work may already be mutating state. |
23: | `completed` | The turn reached a reported stop reason. |
24: | `unknown` | Partial mutation cannot be ruled out. |
25: 
26: Runner never auto-falls back or resends, and never restarts or resumes a session on its own. Read the receipt and decide whether another prompt is appropriate.
27: 
28: ## Communication loop
29: 
30: Resolve this Skill's installed directory once and call its scripts by absolute path — the install
31: destination may contain spaces, and the user's project is passed only through `--repo` (relative
32: paths in these references resolve against the Skill, never the project cwd). Progressive
33: disclosure: open a reference only when the current operation needs it, run the scripts and never read their source, and prefer bounded
34: receipts (`observe`, `status`, `capture --lines`) over whole-history dumps — `capture --full` is an
35: explicit, unbounded request:
36: 
37: ```bash
38: SKILL_DIR="/absolute/path/to/dsh-kaola-project-runner"   # the directory containing this file
39: REPO="/abs/canonical/root"   # canonical Git root, not a linked worktree
40: SESSION="<exact-name>"   # under Project Runner: <platform>-<CODE>-i<ISSUE>-<purpose>
41: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" preflight --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
42: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" start --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
43: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" observe --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
44: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" capture --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --lines 200
45: ```
46: 
47: The controlling Agent owns model selection for each `start`. This Skill declares its per-run
48: presets — `--tier default` (**DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**: `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, no Runner effort override) only — and `default` applies whenever nothing more specific was chosen. Pass
49: another `--tier` when the human or an existing authorization — the default-authorized Worker pool included —
50: names that preset; never infer one from code size, failures, elapsed time, or your own assessment.
51: An undeclared name is refused (`tier-not-declared`), never resolved to `default`.
52: 
53: An explicit user model choice always wins: pass it with `--model ID`, adding `--effort LEVEL` only
54: when the user also named an effort. A bare explicit `--model` leaves the runtime's native effort
55: alone — never attach a preset's effort to a different model. If the user picks a model ID that
56: already encodes effort or Fast (such as a `-fast` variant), pass it as-is; the Runner does not
57: invent extra effort or Fast configuration for it.
58: 
59: Fast is OFF by default. Pass `--fast on` only on an explicit user request for Fast; this platform's
60: Fast support: no native Fast toggle and no Fast config option on the ACP surface; the catalog's flash-named routes are explicit model choices, not a Fast switch. Fast and tier are independent selections. When a native fast model
61: ID is what the user explicitly selected, it counts as the explicit Fast selection — report the
62: conflict honestly if it is also passed with `--fast off`.
63: 
64: `preflight` and `start` report the requested and resolved selection, and `start` what it applied
65: (`config_application`, `effective_selection`), including unavailable, unsupported, and unknown
66: outcomes; `observe`/`status` show the agent's `configOptions` `currentValue`. `--resume`/`--continue`
67: preserve the saved native session model and effort unless the caller supplies `--tier`, `--model`,
68: or `--effort`; Fast stays a per-run request (off unless explicitly on). All of this is per-run
69: input and never rewrites global CLI configuration. A mismatch or unreadable actual model remains
70: evidence for the Agent and does not disable the communication channel.
71: 
72: `preflight` reports runtime and optional Kaola carrier evidence. Missing Workflow commands,
73: configuration health, account state, activity hints, or a changed
74: snapshot do not authorize or block starting the CLI communication channel.
75: 
76: Use the evidence internally to choose the next communication action. Do not narrate raw holder,
77: process, snapshot, model, or activity fields in user progress updates; report only visible
78: task progress, an actual transport failure, or a decision that genuinely needs the user.
79: 
80: After reading current evidence, the controlling Agent chooses what to send:
81: 
82: ```bash
83: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" send --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --text '<agent-selected prompt>'
84: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" observe --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
85: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" capture --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --lines 200
86: ```
87: 
88: ## Steering a running turn
89: 
90: dsh's ACP surface exposes no native mid-turn entry, so a bare `steer`
91: refuses and writes nothing. The available path is the composite, which you
92: choose explicitly:
93: 
94: ```bash
95: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" steer --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" \
96:   --steer-mode interrupt --text '<redirection>'
97: ```
98: 
99: It **cancels** the running turn, confirms it stopped, then sends your text as the
100: next turn on the same session, which keeps the conversation's context. That is
101: interrupted-then-continued, never injection: work in progress stops and may have
102: left partial side effects (`side_effects_possible`). An unconfirmed cancel sends
103: nothing and reports `unknown`. See [references/steering.md](references/steering.md).
104: 
105: ## Cancel and permissions
106: 
107: `key --key escape` (or `cancel`) cancels the running turn; there are no other native keys, menus,
108: or editor replacement. Settle a pending permission `request_id` with
109: `permit [--request-id ID] --option OPTION_ID` (an option the request offers); omitting `--option`
110: answers `cancelled`, which denies. Read the resulting output before choosing another action.
111: 
112: Permission default: `start` launches with `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access` (no Seatbelt sandbox, approval never) unless the caller set that variable; `--permission-mode read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access` wins over both (bypassPermissions maps to danger-full-access).
113: 
114: When the Agent decides the exact session is finished, end only that owned session:
115: 
116: ```bash
117: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" stop --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
118: "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" status --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
119: ```
120: 
121: Use `--force` only when the Agent explicitly chooses forced containment for this exact owned
122: session. Never use broad session/process cleanup, and never reconstruct ownership from process
123: names or fuzzy session matches.
124: 
125: ## Ending, releasing, and resuming
126: 
127: The controlling Agent owns every completion judgment; the Runner executes the chosen operation
128: and reports the true result. These are operation facts, never gates:
129: 
130: - A finished reply is not a finished task: an `end_turn` event, an idle terminal, or a
131:   successful `send` receipt never establishes completion.
132: - `stop` releases the owned runtime (the ACP holder and its agent). It never deletes CLI
133:   history, session records, work artifacts, or unrelated resources. Judge success by the
134:   `stop`/`status` result evidence, not by a completed call.
135: - Before stopping, the Agent may keep available resume facts (platform, canonical repo, any
136:   reported native session ID, outcome, remaining work) from existing receipts and Workflow
137:   records. The native session ID is the CLI's own conversation identifier, never the Runner's
138:   `--session` name. Missing identifiers never block a chosen `stop`.
139: - Later work resumes by the Agent's choice: `start --resume <native-session-id>`,
140:   `start --continue` for the platform's latest conversation, or a fresh `start` plus existing
141:   records where the platform cannot resume.
142: 
143: ## Optional Kaola Workflow
144: 
145: Ordinary Workflow-backed work binds `--repo` to the consuming project's canonical Git root and asks this CLI to invoke its installed
146: `workflow-next`, so that runtime's Workflow creates or recovers the child worktree; this Skill only
147: transports the exact session. Linked-worktree starts, outer-prepared bundles, and existing-run
148: recovery are Agent decisions, not transport gates. A session already in a child worktree is advisory: preserve work, then continue,
149: stop/restart at root, or use another Workflow recovery path. Installation for another runtime alone
150: does not establish availability here.
151: 
152: ## Evidence boundary
153: 
154: - `capture`, events, process facts, permission facts, activity hints, and snapshot changes are
155:   evidence for the Agent.
156: - Exact session ownership, platform/repository identity, holder identity, prompt fingerprinting,
157:   and outbound redaction are transport integrity checks.
158: - The Runner never classifies evidence into permission to act. The Agent handles every runtime or
159:   Workflow problem after reading the evidence.
160: - No invocation implicitly starts `workflow-next`, installs commands, materializes repository files,
161:   creates a heartbeat, or selects recurring behavior. The Agent may send any of those commands when
162:   it decides they serve the user's task.
163: 
164: See [references/platform.md](references/platform.md) for dsh launch/observation facts
165: and [references/acp.md](references/acp.md) for the structured ACP command surface.

1: # Sideagent nodes, results and Host continuity
2: 
3: `S` is the `state` command of [lifecycle-state.md](lifecycle-state.md);
4: `execute` and `collect` are in [dispatch-collect.md](dispatch-collect.md).
5: 
6: ## Implementation items
7: 
8: `scope: implementation` is the only scope that admits `mutation: true`.
9: `execute` claims nothing, makes no worktree and touches no forge: the worker's
10: Workflow owns that. Each item sends either its own `prompt` exactly, or the
11: plan's `core` (with `core_revision`) plus the item's `worker_scope`, joined by
12: one blank line; never both. The index row's `prompt_source` keeps the kind,
13: core revision and `sha256:` of core, scope and sent prompt.
14: 
15: With `--state FILE`, an item's `task_id` adds its id to that task's
16: `dispatch` (writer `tool:execute`, no Host revision); an unknown task is
17: `evidence.task_note`. A hold naming the item's `preset` (or `presets`) makes
18: it `not-run` / `on-hold` before any Runner call: a known hold is not probed
19: again. An exactly reconciled prior item stays reconciled.
20: 
21: ## Results
22: 
23: A `collect` result has `excerpt` (480 characters) with `excerpt_truncated`
24: and `reply_chars`; `turn` (holder, prompt fingerprint); `locator` (the Runner
25: `capture` argv `--since <dispatch cursor> --full --inline` and the event log);
26: `output` with its `kind`: `file` (a path, or `{"path": ...}`; checked for
27: presence), `capture` (the reply itself), `remote` (a URL) or `description`
28: (text with spaces); an explicit `{"kind": ...}` wins; and `gaps`:
29: `reply-text-absent`, `capture-truncated`, `output-absent` (a file only). A gap is evidence,
30: not a transport failure. Read the full reply through `locator` before a
31: verdict. A new return resets `acceptance` to `pending` and keeps the earlier
32: value as `prior_acceptance`.
33: 
34: ## Per-assignment dispositions
35: 
36: Task `dispositions` maps item id to `accepted`, `repair`, `cancelled`,
37: `superseded` or `handed-off`. It is Host-owned like `verdict`, which stays the
38: task-level judgment. `$S update --kind tasks ... --index I` mirrors them to the
39: index `acceptance` with `acceptance_source`. After a task verdict, an item of
40: that task without a disposition becomes `undecided` with a note, never left
41: `pending`. A mirror error is reported; the state write stands.
42: 
43: ## Host revision
44: 
45: Each Host business write raises the file's `host_revision` and stamps the
46: record. Tool and Sideagent writes raise nothing and stamp `writer_holder`. The
47: Sideagent view lists `pending_host_changes`: `host:<kind>/<id>@<rev>`,
48: `host:section/<name>@<rev>` and `host:retired/<kind>/<id>@<rev>`.
49: 
50: ## Node mode
51: 
52: Bind `--section sideagent` with `"mode": "node"` and
53: `"recipe": {"runner": "<absolute Runner file>", "argv": ["start", "--repo",
54: "<root>", "--session", "<bound name>", "--role", "sideagent", ...]}` (the
55: checkout `kaola-tmux.sh` takes the platform before `start`), without
56: `--continue` or `--resume` (an optional absolute `state_tool` names
57: `kaola-dispatch.py` when it is not beside the holder or in the sibling Skill). Worker
58: returns and terminations are not node inputs: they reach the Host at its next
59: idle boundary as without a binding, and the Host reads the original. A Host
60: holder advertising `sideagent-node/1` starts a node only for Host business
61: changes past the handled revision, selected when the Host turn has ended, so
62: one turn's writes are one batch. It starts one fresh node from that argv (no
63: shell), sends one prompt with the batch id, the Host revision range and the
64: node's role limits (source pointers only, no restated result, no dispatch or
65: judgment, exact-stop only a Host-recorded reclaim), and reads the node's checkpoint at its turn end. A turn end alone
66: acknowledges nothing. A refused recipe is logged once.
67: 
68: The node writes once:
69: 
70: ```bash
71: $S checkpoint --writer sideagent --source B --batch B --through-host-revision R \
72:   --entries '[{"input":"<id>","applied":["tasks/t1"]},{"input":"<id>","retained":"tasks/t2"}]'
73: ```
74: 
75: `applied` names current records, or `retired:<kind>/<id>`, that this node's
76: holder wrote. `retained` names a current record with `next`, `owner` or `wait`,
77: or a Host `section/<name>`. Older or foreign evidence settles nothing. The
78: result is `maintenance.last_checkpoint`; `last_verified` moves only when every
79: input settled. `acked_host_revision` never passes an unsettled change; a later
80: Host write stays pending. An input the Host rewrote during the batch is
81: `superseded`: its rewrite is the next batch's input. Unsettled inputs go to the Host once, in one
82: `maintenance-returned` alert, and are never sent to another node.
83: 
84: After a verified batch the carrier wakes the Host once, at its next idle
85: boundary, only when an attention item is a record this node wrote and the
86: Host view's attention differs both from what the Host last saw and from the
87: batch's start; otherwise it stays quiet. A partial or
88: missing checkpoint, one whose `through` is below the batch's range, a refused
89: batch, a failed start or a lost node reaches the Host once with the unhandled
90: range; the carrier then exact-stops the node by holder and starts no node for
91: that range again. A failed start or refused batch starts no further node until
92: the binding changes. After `sideagent_node_stop_unconfirmed` no node starts
93: while that holder process still runs. A Host stop in any mode also stops its
94: own node, a start in flight included. A replaced node's late write is
95: `binding-superseded`. There is no timer: the next Host change starts the next
96: node at a Host turn end or the existing idle tick.
97: 
98: ## Host continuity stop
99: 
100: `stop` or `drain-restart` with `--preserve-dispatched-workers` on a Host whose
101: holder advertises `preserve-dispatched/1` keeps each worker tree that Host
102: dispatched (spawn line or a worker record naming its holder) on a cooperative
103: or dead-holder stop; other children are still swept. An older live holder
104: refuses with `preserve-unsupported` and stops nothing: `drain-restart` it at
105: idle first. The successor then runs each seat's `rebind-host`. A start still in
106: flight is not covered: reconcile it. Default stop and final close-out are
107: unchanged; close-out reclaims workers one by one first.
108: 
109: ## Idle wake
110: 
111: A worker's undelivered `idle` wake to its Host is kept like a permission wake
112: and re-sent when the Host is reachable; a newer one replaces it and a stop
113: drops it.

116: preserve stop and rebind on both, and a model-driven Codex Host with a Codex
117: node binding.
